climate_pressure: Sea-level/storm-surge pressures and reported changes in coastal water/livelihood conditions.
documented_impact: The Tandubas workshop case describes salinity/freshwater losses, affected fishing/seaweed livelihoods and movement inland.
fcv_mediator: Inland settlement encountering ancestral sites and contested land/cultural rights.
possible_consequence: Participants linked this to disputes, cultural conflict and crime/violence; no incidence estimate or causal identification.
alternative_explanations: Pre-existing land rights, historical injustice, governance, livelihood change and settlement pressures independently shape conflict.
uncertainty: A 2023 workshop case, not representative or independently causal evidence. Local/Indigenous/vulnerable residents were not adequately represented; no current violence map or attribution of individual events to anthropogenic change. Not independently reverified in the 27 October 2026 remediation; check the cited passage before relying on this claim.
resilience_factors: Inclusive land-use dialogue and protection of rights are relevant safeguards; the workshop does not evaluate their delivery or peace effects.
compact_statement: The 2023 Tandubas workshop account links coastal livelihood/water pressures and inland movement with ancestral-site disputes; it is a low-confidence, source-stated local mechanism, not a measured climate effect on violence.
